question: A conductor is connected to a battery of 6V. Let V₁ be the potential difference across the conductor. When a battery of 9 V is connected, the potential difference becomes V₂ · (V₁ / V₂) is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2/3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The potential difference across a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage applied.**
 
• Given a 6V battery, let the potential difference be V1.
 
• When a 9V battery is connected, the potential difference becomes V2.
 
• According to Ohm's Law, V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3" id="MathJax-Element-4-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">[Math Processing Error]V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3" id="MathJax-Element-46-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3 V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3 V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3 V1/V2=6V/9V=2/3 V1/V2 = 6V/9V = 2/3 .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• It is usually formulated as V=IR" id="MathJax-Element-5-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IRV=IR" id="MathJax-Element-2-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IRV=IR" id="MathJax-Element-47-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IRV=IR" id="MathJax-Element-12-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IRV=IR" id="MathJax-Element-14-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IRV=IR" id="MathJax-Element-22-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IRV=IR" id="MathJax-Element-26-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IRV=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR V = IR , where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• This relationship implies that as the voltage increases, the potential difference across the conductor increases proportionally if the resistance remains constant.
